hot.pointer_line: On now: a glut of palamut, a thin lüfer run and the first hamsi, boza returning, sunsets sliding from 18:23 to 17:45, Republic Day on 29 October, the marathon on 1 November, the 09:05 silence on 10 November and İKSV's theatre festival from 22 October.

items.name: Palamut in a glut year
items.teaser: The 2026 season opened on 1 September with more palamut than the Istanbul fish market has seen in years
items.story: Commercial fishing reopened on 1 September 2026 and the palamut came with it, south through the strait from the Black Sea. Cumhuriyet called it the most plentiful season in years. The Istanbul fish market's figures for the first week of September put 750-850 gram fish at 59 to 71 lira a kilo, after 150-200 lira on the opening days, and Dünya noted it selling at half the price of minced beef. By late autumn the bigger fish are called torik. Buy it whole, have it gutted at the counter, and grill it the same day: the oil that makes it good also turns it fast.
items.why: In a glut year palamut is the cheapest good fish in the city: eat it grilled, or as lakerda later in the winter.
facts: Season from 1 Sep 2026; palamut through autumn, torik as the fish grow
Kadıköy and Karaköy fish counters; Istanbul fish market at Gürpınar for the trade
Wholesale 59-71 TL/kg for 750-850 g fish, first week of Sep 2026; retail higher
Ask for it 'temizlensin', cleaned at the counter, and look for bright eyes and red gills

items.name: Lüfer, scarce and dear
items.teaser: The strait's prized bluefish has not come in strongly this autumn, and the price shows it
items.story: Lüfer is the fish Istanbul argues about. Its names are sizes: the İstanbul Ansiklopedisi lists defne yaprağı, çinakop, sarıkanat, then lüfer proper at two to nine fish a kilo, and kofana above a kilo each. Posta reported that the Marmara catch had not reached the plenty of last year and that prices had climbed. The legal landing size is the other argument: press accounts give 20 cm, cut to 18 cm in the 2016-2020 rules, and inspectors still seize crates of 14-15 cm fish. A real lüfer, grilled whole over charcoal, is a size well above the legal line. Ask what it weighed.
items.why: Order a lüfer by the size name; a plate of small çinekop is the fish the conservationists want left in the water.
facts: Autumn into early winter; 2026 run reported weak so far
Strait-side fish restaurants and the Kadıköy fish row
No 2026 price found; expect it above palamut
Refuse çinekop under the legal size, given in press as 18-20 cm

items.name: The first hamsi
items.teaser: Hamsi hit Istanbul stalls in September at about 200 lira a kilo; the Black Sea shoals are still to come
items.story: Hamsi is the Black Sea's winter fish, and the city waits for it. Around 20 September 2026 the Istanbul stalls were selling it at about 200 lira a kilo, with some first-day prices up to 250, according to 24 Saat. Trabzon fishermen said at the end of September that the local Black Sea hamsi had not yet come in properly and that part of what was on sale was from the Marmara. Prices fall as the shoals arrive and jump again when storms keep the boats in. The fried hamsi tava, the pilaf, and hamsi cooked under cornbread belong to the cold months.
items.why: Wait for the price to fall: that is the sign the Black Sea shoals have arrived and the fish is at its fattest.
facts: First fish Sep 2026; full Black Sea run usually from late autumn into winter
Every fish counter; Black Sea lokantas such as Hayvore off İstiklal
About 200 TL/kg retail, around 20 Sep 2026; up to 250 TL on opening days
Small, stiff and shining: buy it the morning it lands and fry it the same day

items.name: The light goes early
items.teaser: Mid-October sunsets are near 18:23; by mid-November the sun is down by 17:45, and earlier still to December
items.story: Turkey stays on UTC+3 all year, so there is no clock change at the end of October to soften the shift. On 15 October the sun sets in Istanbul at about 18:23 after 11 hours and 8 minutes of daylight. On 15 November it sets at about 17:45, with under ten hours of day, and the evenings keep shortening into December. For a deck, that means a sunset drink on the strait now comes before dinner, not with it. The low autumn sun sits over the European shore in the late afternoon and lights the Asian side's waterfront houses from Kuzguncuk to Kandilli.
items.why: Plan the Bosphorus cruise for mid-afternoon: by November the light is gone before 18:00.
facts: Sunset about 18:23 on 15 Oct and 17:45 on 15 Nov 2026 (local time, UTC+3)
Best seen from the Asian shore, looking west to the old city
No clock change in Turkey: phone calendars set to European time will be an hour off after 25 Oct

items.name: Lodos and poyraz
items.teaser: The southwester and the northeaster are the two winds that cancel Istanbul's ferries from autumn on
items.story: Two winds rule the strait. Lodos comes from the southwest off the Marmara: warm, gusty and wet, it piles water against the European shore and has stopped Şehir Hatları and İDO ferries many times, most recently in January 2026. Poyraz blows cold from the northeast down the Bosphorus from the Black Sea and has cancelled İDO sailings too. In November 2025 bad weather halted ferries and the ministry suspended ship traffic through the strait in both directions. A lodos day in autumn can feel almost warm on land while the island boats sit tied up. Check the operators before a Princes' Islands day.
items.why: On a lodos day, keep the plan on one shore and use the Marmaray tunnel or a bridge to cross.
facts: Any time from autumn to spring; no forecast for specific 2026 dates
Marmara crossings and the island lines first; the Bosphorus lines later
Şehir Hatları and İDO post cancellations on their own sites and accounts the same morning

items.name: Two full moons and two showers
items.teaser: Full moon 26 Oct at 07:12 and 24 Nov at 17:53 Istanbul time; Orionids peak 21-22 Oct, Leonids 17-18 Nov
items.story: The October full moon falls at 04:12 UTC on 26 October, which is 07:12 in Istanbul, so it sets over the European shore at dawn. November's is at 14:53 UTC on 24 November, 17:53 local time, and rises out of Asia just as it gets dark: a full moon over the Bosphorus bridge for anyone on the water that evening. The Orionids, dust from Halley's Comet, peak on the night of 21-22 October, best after the moon sets. The Leonids peak on the night of 17-18 November. City light will cut both to a handful an hour; the Black Sea end of the strait is darker.
items.why: The 24 November moonrise is the one to plan a boat evening around.
facts: Full moon Mon 26 Oct 07:12 and Tue 24 Nov 17:53 (UTC+3); Orionids night of 21-22 Oct; Leonids night of 17-18 Nov
The Bosphorus, facing east for moonrise; Rumeli Kavağı end for darker sky

items.name: Boza is back
items.teaser: Thick, sour-sweet fermented millet with cinnamon and roasted chickpeas: the cold-season glass returns
items.story: Boza is fermented millet, thick enough to eat with a spoon, sour and sweet at once, dusted with cinnamon and served with a dish of roasted chickpeas, leblebi, to drop in. It is a winter drink: the street sellers' cry of 'bozaaa' used to mean the cold had come. Vefa Bozacısı has poured it from the same counter near the Süleymaniye since 1876, and still shows a glass Atatürk drank from. One source says the shop shuts from June to September and sells şıra, grape must, in the warm months. October is when the boza comes back; confirm the date before you climb the hill.
items.why: Drink it standing at the Vefa counter, with leblebi bought from the shop across the street.
facts: Cold season, about October to spring; 2026 reopening date not confirmed
Ask for it 'tarçınlı, leblebili': with cinnamon and chickpeas

items.name: Chestnuts and new walnuts
items.teaser: The street carts start roasting kestane as the weather turns, and the 2026 walnut harvest is in
items.story: The chestnut carts appear on Istanbul's corners when the first cold evenings come, roasting kestane over coals and selling them by the paper bag; the same nuts go into kestane şekeri, candied chestnut from Bursa. Turkish press reported the season's first chestnuts reaching market at prices that raised eyebrows. Dünya reported in 2026 that the new walnut harvest had begun after a 2025 frost cut the national crop from about 426,000 tonnes to about 263,000. New walnuts are pale and sweet, and appear in the markets' sacks through the autumn, alongside the year's first dried figs and apricots.
items.why: Buy a bag from a cart on a cold evening and eat them walking, before they go hard.
facts: Chestnuts from October as the weather cools; new walnuts from the autumn harvest
Street carts in Eminönü, Taksim and Kadıköy; market sacks for walnuts
Pick a cart with a queue: the chestnuts there have not sat on the coals

items.name: Quince and pomegranate
items.teaser: Quince for ayva tatlısı, pomegranate for the molasses: the two fruits of an Istanbul autumn
items.story: In October the greengrocers' crates fill with yellow quince and split red pomegranates. Quince is too hard to eat raw; it is poached into ayva tatlısı, halves cooked with sugar and their own seeds until they turn deep red, then topped with kaymak. Pomegranate is pressed for juice on the street from portable presses and boiled down into nar ekşisi, the sour molasses that dresses salads and the kısır of the southeast. Both keep through the winter, so the season runs long. Buy quince heavy and fragrant; buy pomegranates with hard, tight skins that feel heavy for their size.
items.why: Order ayva tatlısı with kaymak at a lokanta: it is the dessert that says the season has turned.
facts: Greengrocers in the Kadıköy market; street juice presses
Check the label on nar ekşisi: the real one lists only pomegranate

items.name: Republic Day and 10 November
items.teaser: 29 Oct, a Thursday, is a holiday with flags on the bridges; at 09:05 on 10 Nov the whole city stands still
items.story: The Republic was proclaimed on 29 October 1923, and the day is a public holiday; this year it falls on a Thursday, with the afternoon of 28 October off. In 2025 the 15 Temmuz Şehitler, Fatih Sultan Mehmet and Yavuz Sultan Selim bridges were hung with Turkish flags, and the city has staged fireworks over the Bosphorus in past years; the 2026 programme is not yet out. On Tuesday 10 November, at 09:05, the minute Atatürk died in Dolmabahçe Palace in 1938, sirens sound and traffic, ferries and people stop for a minute's silence. It is not a holiday: offices and shops open.
items.why: At 09:05 on 10 November, stop where you are; the room where he died at Dolmabahçe fills with carnations.
facts: Thu 29 Oct 2026 (half day 28 Oct); Tue 10 Nov 2026, 09:05
Citywide; state ceremonies at Taksim Republic Monument; Dolmabahçe Palace on 10 Nov
Expect the 15 Temmuz bridge and Taksim to close at set hours; check the Valilik notice

items.name: Istanbul Marathon, Sunday 1 November
items.teaser: The 48th edition starts on the Asian side, crosses the 15 Temmuz bridge and finishes in Sultanahmet
items.story: The Istanbul Marathon is the one race that starts in Asia and finishes in Europe. The 48th edition runs on Sunday 1 November 2026: the field crosses the 15 Temmuz Şehitler bridge, closed to traffic for the morning, then follows the European shore to finish at the Hippodrome in Sultanahmet. It carries a World Athletics Gold Label. Even for those not running, it shapes the day: the bridge and the shore roads close, and thousands join the shorter fun run across the bridge on foot. A single travel listing gives 2 November; the race calendars give the 1st.
items.why: Cross the bridge with the fun run: it is the one morning a year you can walk it.
facts: Start on the Asian side of the 15 Temmuz bridge; finish at the Hippodrome, Sultanahmet

items.name: 30th Istanbul Theatre Festival
items.teaser: Seventeen productions on both sides of the city for İKSV's 30th theatre festival, through 3 December
items.story: İKSV's theatre festival reaches its 30th edition this autumn, chosen by Mehmet Birkiye, running from 22 October to 3 December 2026. The programme has 17 theatre, performance and dance pieces, six from abroad and eleven from Turkey, spread across 17 venues on both shores of the city, and closes with a staging of The Picture of Dorian Gray. A free side programme, Festival Artı, began in September. Some productions are in Turkish only; the foreign companies usually perform in their own language with surtitles. Tickets sell out for the visiting companies first.
items.why: Pick one of the six visiting productions and book now: they play few nights.
facts: 17 venues on both sides of the city

items.name: Ramadan and Ramazan Bayramı, 2027
items.teaser: Ramadan expected 8 February to 8 March 2027, with the bayram on 9-11 March
items.story: Ramadan 2027 is expected to begin on Monday 8 February, ending on 8 March, with Ramazan Bayramı, also called Şeker Bayramı, on Tuesday 9 to Thursday 11 March; the afternoon of 8 March is the arife half day. Turkish holiday calendars from CNN Türk and others agree on these dates; Diyanet's lunar calendar fixes them. In Istanbul restaurants and bars stay open in daylight, but the city changes shape at dusk: iftar tables fill the squares near Sultanahmet and Eyüp, and the drummer walks the streets before dawn. During the bayram itself, many lokantas close and the roads out of the city jam.
items.why: Book any table for iftar hour well ahead; it is the busiest sitting of the day.
facts: Ramadan about 8 Feb-8 Mar 2027; bayram 9-11 Mar 2027 (half day 8 Mar)
Citywide; Sultanahmet and Eyüp most visibly at iftar

items.name: Kurban Bayramı, 2027
items.teaser: The four-day sacrifice feast runs 16-19 May 2027, after a half-day arife on Saturday 15 May
items.story: Kurban Bayramı is the longest religious holiday of the Turkish year: four days, from Sunday 16 to Wednesday 19 May 2027, with the afternoon of Saturday 15 May off. In 2026 it fell on 27-30 May; it moves about eleven days earlier each year. Families who can afford it have a sheep or a share of a cow sacrificed and give much of the meat away. For a visitor the effect is practical: offices, banks and many family restaurants shut, half the city leaves, and the motorways and airports are at their busiest on the days either side.
items.why: Provision a boat before the arife: wholesale suppliers close for the whole feast.
facts: Expect Istanbul's own roads to empty and the airport to fill

items.name: Republic Day, every 29 October
items.teaser: Every 29 October the city flies the flag from the bridges and the state holds its ceremony in Taksim
items.story: The Republic of Turkey was proclaimed on 29 October 1923 and the date is the country's main civic holiday, with the afternoon of 28 October off. Flags go up on the Bosphorus bridges, the state lays wreaths at the Republic Monument in Taksim, and in many years the city has put on fireworks and light shows over the water between the Bosphorus bridge and Kız Kulesi. In 2027, 29 October falls on a Friday, making a long weekend. Ten days later, on 10 November, the country stops at 09:05 for Atatürk.
items.why: If you are on the water on the night of the 29th, ask the captain where the fireworks will be.
facts: 29 Oct every year; 2027 a Friday (half day Thu 28 Oct)
Citywide; Taksim and the Bosphorus shore
The programme and bridge closures are announced a few days before

items.name: Istanbul Film Festival
items.teaser: İKSV's film festival fills the Beyoğlu cinemas for twelve days every April
items.story: İKSV's Istanbul Film Festival is the city's spring cinema fortnight and has run in April for years: 17-28 April in 2024, 11-22 April in 2025 and 9-19 April for the 45th edition in 2026, which opened with 127 films. Screenings fill the Beyoğlu cinemas and the Atlas, with Turkish and international competitions, and Turkish films are generally shown with English subtitles. The 2027 dates have not been announced. Tickets go on sale shortly before the festival and the evening screenings with directors present sell out first.
items.why: Pick a Turkish competition film with English subtitles: it is the best view of the country's new cinema.
facts: Book the director nights the day sales open

items.name: İKSV's summer: music and jazz
items.teaser: The Istanbul Music Festival in June, then the Istanbul Jazz Festival in July, both run by İKSV
items.story: İKSV, the foundation behind the film and theatre festivals, runs two summer music festivals. The Istanbul Music Festival, classical music in the city's historic halls and churches, usually takes June. The Istanbul Jazz Festival follows in July, with open-air concerts and club nights across the city. Neither has announced its 2027 dates. A separate event, the Akbank Jazz Festival, is the autumn one: its 36th edition ran from 26 September to 11 October 2026, with more than 30 concerts, so it has just ended. Book İKSV summer concerts when the programme is published in spring.
items.why: A classical concert in Hagia Irene during the music festival is the one to try for.
facts: Music Festival usually June; Jazz Festival usually July; 2027 dates not announced
The Akbank Jazz Festival is the autumn one: late September to mid-October

items.name: Tulips at Emirgan
items.teaser: Every April the city plants millions of tulips, and Emirgan Grove on the Bosphorus is the heart of it
items.story: The tulip came to Europe from the Ottoman court, and the city celebrates it each April with the Istanbul Tulip Festival, planting beds in its parks and squares. Emirgan Grove, on the European shore of the Bosphorus north of the second bridge, is the main show, with beds laid out in patterns down the slopes to the water. Bloom depends on the weather: early April after a mild winter, later after a cold one. Weekends are crowded; a weekday morning gives the gardens almost to yourself. Emirgan Sütiş on the waterfront below is the breakfast stop.
items.why: Go on a weekday morning, then take breakfast with kaymak on the Emirgan waterfront.
facts: Check the bloom reports in late March before fixing a day

items.name: Hıdırellez, 5-6 May
items.teaser: The night of 5-6 May, when Hızır and İlyas meet, people tie wishes to trees and jump fires
items.story: Hıdırellez marks the meeting of the prophets Hızır and İlyas, and with it the start of summer, on the night of 5 to 6 May. People write or tie wishes to the branches of rose bushes and trees, leave them overnight, and jump bonfires for luck; the Romani quarters of the city have long made the most of it, with music through the night. UNESCO inscribed the Spring Celebration, Hıdrellez, on its intangible heritage list in December 2017 as a joint file of Turkey and North Macedonia. It is a folk celebration, not a holiday, and the timing is fixed.
items.why: Look for the Romani music nights of 5 May in the old city's neighbourhoods.
facts: Bring a ribbon: the wish tree is the point

items.name: Swimming the Bosphorus
items.teaser: Once a year the strait closes to ships and a few thousand swimmers cross from Asia to Europe
items.story: The Bosphorus Cross-Continental Swim, run by the Turkish Olympic Committee since 1989, closes the strait to shipping for a morning while swimmers go from the Asian shore at Kanlıca to Kuruçeşme on the European side, about 6.5 km with the current. The first race in 1989 was in July, and that is the month many guides still give, but recent editions have moved to late August: 25 August in 2024, and the 38th set for 23 August 2026 by one news report. Places are limited. Spectators line the Kuruçeşme shore.
items.why: Watch the finish from Kuruçeşme: it is the one morning the strait is empty of ships.
facts: Late summer; 2026 reported as 23 Aug; 2027 not announced

items.name: The fishing year
items.teaser: Commercial fishing runs 1 September to 15 April: in summer most fish on ice is farmed
items.story: Turkey's fishing year sets the city's menus. The general ban lifts on 1 September, as it did in 2026, and the palamut runs come first, then lüfer through the autumn and hamsi from late autumn into winter. On 15 April the commercial boats stop again until September, to let the fish spawn, and from then until the end of August most of what is on the ice is farmed levrek and çipura or brought in from elsewhere. A summer menu offering wild lüfer deserves a question. Lakerda, the cured torik, carries the autumn into the winter.
items.why: Come in autumn to eat the Bosphorus fish; in summer, ask whether the fish is farmed.
facts: Season 1 Sep-15 Apr; closed 15 Apr-31 Aug
Every fish counter in the city
In summer, ask 'kültür mü, deniz mi?': farmed or wild?
